newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: UNIONS EXPECT ANOTHER 2,500 JOBS TO BE CUT AT PHILIPS.
newsitem.headline: UNIONS EXPECT ANOTHER 2,500 JOBS TO BE CUT AT PHILIPS.

text.p: The FNV Industry union said on Thursday it expected Philips Electronics NV to shed another 2,500 jobs in the Netherlands, after the firm reported a sharp drop in third quarter earnings.
"The 2,500 job losses we foresee come on top of the 1,000 jobs which will be scrapped under a previously announced reorganisation," a union spokeswoman said.
She said the union had begun its calculations when Philips warned last week that profits would be lower and that today's figures supported the idea that more jobs would have to go.
Philips said today it expected to take a reorganisation charge of one billion guilders in the fourth quarter of 1996.
The union spokeswoman noted that for Operation Centurion, a big reorganisation launched in the early 1990s, Philips had set aside four billion guilders and 10,000 jobs had been cut.
Another official of the same union, Jan Couperus, said the job cuts were likely to fall at the lighting, semiconductor & components businesses and at the head office in Eindhoven.
Couperus said he did not know how quickly the job cuts would be implemented but added: "(New chairman Cor) Boonstra is in a hurry." -- Amsterdam newsroom +31 20 504 5000
